newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey postpones rise in port fees until June.
newsitem.headline: Turkey postpones rise in port fees until June.

text.p: Turkey on Thursday postponed a rise of up to 170 percent in port and container service fees in seven leading ports after protests by exporters, a senior official said.
"We have postponed the fee increase decision to the beginning of June," Oguz Tezmen, transport ministry undersecretary, told Reuters.
"We will bring together all related parties to the issue and try to find a formula that will please all," he said.
Exporters had threatened to stop shipments unless the government backed down.
Tezmem said the fee increases were meant to help reduce the losses of the Turkish Railways Authority (TCDD) port operator. These amounted to an estimated 60 trillion lira in 1996.
Mahmut Arslan, head of the Mediterranean Grain and Pulses Exporters Union, based in Mersin, said the trade would cancel the plan to halt shipments from the port.
"We will not stop exports on May 6 now that the government has withdrawn fee hikes for one month. I hope they will find a reasonable solution to the problem," he said.
In February TCDD, which operates the seven biggest ports in Turkey, raised fees for port services to $8.3 per tonne from $5 and empty container services to $35 per tonne from $13.
Mersin, one of the seven ports operated by TCDD, handles about 11 million tonnes of incoming and outgoing cargo each year, including one million tonnes of pulses.
About $9 billion, or one-sixth, of Turkey's entire annual trade is carried out through Mersin.
Arslan said the planed increase in fees would undermine plans to boost Turkey's entire exports to $28 billion in 1997 from an estimated $20 billion in 1996.
